correctness.rationale: The finite positive killed-chain eigenvector yields the characteristic identity for every k. The positive change of variables r=q/lambda is an increasing bijection; the derivative of h_m has one strictly monotone sign crossing, proving the unique optimizer. A compactness and monotone limiting-equation argument proves both high-k limits. Exact enumeration, rational determinant comparisons and independent Perron power iteration passed 387 regression assertions. Boundary and order-of-limits restrictions are explicit.

originality.rationale: Fu–Wang–Lou (2003) supplies a general fixed-parameter run-distribution/Perron framework, but material inspection of its six scientific sections did not identify optimization of the symmetric equal-marginal transition family, the strictly unique optimal persistence for every run length at least three, or the high-length universal constants. The earlier two-wet-day result is strictly a one-length special case. The result is provisionally original under accessible evidence; uncovered full texts remain a stated risk.
residual_risks: Full text of Koutras (1997) was not retrievable, and an attempted authorized institutional access route reported that the connection was unavailable; its distribution and asymptotic methods could conceal a relevant parameter-optimization corollary.
Older meteorological and longest-run manuscripts, including Weiss (1964), Lou (1996), and Samarova (1982), were accessible only to abstract or bibliographic depth.
General reliability literature might contain a mathematically equivalent sharp spectral-optimization theorem under a different vocabulary.
No independent assessment of historical priority has been performed.

value.rationale: Holding daily wet probability at one half removes marginal frequency as a confounder, while the optimized persistence determines the fastest exponential onset of specified long wet spells. A complete all-length unique-maximizer classification and two nontrivial large-spell scaling constants provide a motivated exact benchmark for binary precipitation-sequence stress testing, beyond the preexisting k=2 special case; no unsupported empirical significance is claimed.
